title: The Last Vector
premise: Ansel Underhill, a clone who inherited the original's unsolved murder case, keeps the records of Meridian Station, a dying colony the Core worlds abandoned decades ago. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries — the tongue of the very people the colony's founders helped exterminate — Ansel discovers the original Underhill was murdered to bury evidence that Meridian's survival depends on stolen alien technology. As rival factions in a brewing war converge on the station, Ansel must decode and deliver the message hidden in the signal: proof that could end the war or ignite it. In the end, Ansel chooses to broadcast the truth at the cost of Meridian's last secret, solving their own murder and finding belonging not in an inherited identity but in the community they chose to save.
about_author: Coral Brightwater is a former marine radio operator who spent six years on remote Arctic stations before turning to fiction, where she writes about isolation, memory, and communities the maps forgot. She lives off-grid with her partner and an unreasonable number of tide charts.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Dead Things
chapters.summary: Ansel Underhill catalogs Meridian Station's failing systems and the cold case file they inherited from their dead original. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as routine, establishing a narrator who records everything because no one else will.

chapters.title: Forty-One Souls
chapters.summary: Ansel walks the station's remaining habitats, interviewing the last colonists for the annual census no one reads. We meet engineer Sefa, doctor Ilya, and matriarch Odile Voss. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: tenderness for a doomed community; the colony is small but fiercely alive.

chapters.title: The Case That Isn't Mine
chapters.summary: Ansel reviews the murder file of the original Ansel Underhill, killed eleven years ago in the reactor annex. The evidence contradicts itself deliberately. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: uncanny grief — mourning a man whose face they wear and whose death they may be meant to repeat.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: A burst transmission hits Meridian's ancient array: structured, repeating, in Kessari — a language extinct since the Purge of two centuries past. Ansel alone recognizes fragments from the case file. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: electric dread; the forgotten past has just knocked.

chapters.title: What Odile Knows
chapters.summary: Ansel brings the recording to Odile Voss, who goes pale and orders it destroyed. She reveals only that the founders 'took something that was never ours.' POV: Ansel, with Odile flashback. Emotional beat: first crack in the colony's shared lie; fear wearing authority's face.

chapters.title: Decomposition of a Lie
chapters.summary: Ansel secretly re-opens the murder case, cross-referencing the signal's timestamp with reactor logs. The original died the night he first decoded a similar fragment. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: cold clarity hardening into purpose — this murder was maintenance of a cover-up.

chapters.title: Sefa's Hands
chapters.summary: Engineer Sefa repairs the deep-array under Ansel's pretext of 'routine calibration,' and admits she's traced the signal's origin: inside the war zone everyone fled from. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: cautious alliance; two keepers of broken things recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The War Comes Closer
chapters.summary: News feeds carry rumors of open hostilities between the Core Compact and the Kessari Remnant fleets. Refugee traffic reroutes away from Meridian — meaning someone knows what's here. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; the galaxy's violence bending toward their small home.

chapters.title: Ilya's Confession
chapters.summary: Doctor Ilya, drunk, tells Ansel the original Underhill treated him the night he died — for burns consistent with alien tech, not reactor coolant. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing after years underwater; the colony's silence was complicity.

chapters.title: The Annex
chapters.summary: Ansel breaks into the sealed reactor annex and finds the original's hidden cache: a Kessari translation matrix and half a message describing 'the debt owed at Meridian.' POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: vertigo of inheritance — the dead original left them a job, not just a face.

chapters.title: Translation, Slowly
chapters.summary: Working nights, Ansel begins decoding the distress signal using the matrix. It is not a plea for rescue — it is a summons naming coordinates beneath Meridian itself. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: dawning horror transformed into terrible wonder; the colony sits on a grave that is still speaking.

chapters.title: Odile's War
chapters.summary: Odile confronts Ansel with a weapon and instead tells the truth: her grandmother led the raid that stole the Kessari vault-core now powering Meridian's shields. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: confession as self-destruction; power confessing its own rot.

chapters.title: The Vault-Core
chapters.summary: Ansel descends into the buried vault and finds the core — alive, humming, wrapped in Kessari script that matches the signal exactly. It isn't stolen machinery. It's a hostage. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: awe curdling into shame; the colony's survival was always ransom.

chapters.title: Visitors
chapters.summary: Two ships arrive unannounced: a Core Compact survey vessel claiming salvage rights, and a scarred Remnant gunship demanding the 'stolen voice' be returned. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the abstract war suddenly standing in the docking bay with guns drawn.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Compact commander Reyes and Remnant captain Ashkav both claim the signal. Ansel stalls by claiming translation authority, buying hours. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into performance; a clerk improvising diplomacy.

chapters.title: Ashkav's Grief
chapters.summary: Alone with Captain Ashkav, Ansel learns the signal came from a Kessari seed-ship, generation-born survivors still singing to their stolen god-machine. POV: Ashkav. Emotional beat: enemy made human through shared loss; grief as common language.

chapters.title: Reyes's Offer
chapters.summary: Commander Reyes privately offers Ansel extraction, wealth, and a new identity if the core goes to the Compact — and hints the original Underhill took a similar deal. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: temptation as mirror; seeing how the original might have died.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone disables the station's comms relay. Sefa finds Compact-made residue — Reyes is cutting Meridian off to take the core quietly. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; the powerful never negotiate when theft will do.

chapters.title: The Colony Votes
chapters.summary: Ansel calls the first full assembly in thirty years and lays out everything: the theft, the signal, the war at the airlock. The forty-one must choose. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: fragile democracy blooming in a dying place; belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Odile's Atonement
chapters.summary: Odile publicly confirms her family's crime and surrenders the founder's codes that control the vault. Some colonists curse her; others weep. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: costly honesty; power finally paying its bill.

chapters.title: The Message Completed
chapters.summary: Using the founder's codes, Ansel unlocks the final segment: the full message is an apology protocol — the core will return willingly if Meridian speaks the founders' confession aloud in Kessari. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: revelation as relief and burden; peace requires the colony to name its sin.

chapters.title: Learning the Dead Language
chapters.summary: Ashkav, against orders, teaches Ansel and volunteer colonists the pronunciation and ritual cadence of the confession rite. POV: Ashkav. Emotional beat: unlikely intimacy; teaching an enemy's tongue becomes an act of hope.

chapters.title: Reyes Moves
chapters.summary: Reyes, tipped off about the rite, seizes the vault entrance and takes Sefa hostage, declaring the core Compact property by salvage law. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: fear and fury; the law arriving as a boot.

chapters.title: The Station Fights Back
chapters.summary: Colonists use intimate knowledge of Meridian's failing systems to trap Reyes's squad in flooded lower decks — the decay itself becomes their defense. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: the weak weaponizing what abandonment left them; grim, triumphant ingenuity.

chapters.title: What Happened to the Original
chapters.summary: In the seized Compact records, Ansel finds the truth: the original Underhill agreed to sell the core, then repented mid-broadcast and was killed by his own Compact handler — Reyes's predecessor. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: closure and warning; the case solves itself as a cautionary tale.

chapters.title: Ansel's Choice
chapters.summary: Reyes offers Ansel the original's exact deal again, now with the colony's evacuation guaranteed — if they abandon the broadcast. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized; survival offered at the price of becoming the murderer's heir in deed.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Ansel refuses publicly, choosing the colony over the exit. Reyes announces she'll take the core by force at dawn. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: resolve settling like bone; fear present but outranked.

chapters.title: Night Before the Rite
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: colonists prepare the vault chamber, mend clothes, write names of their dead. Ansel and Ashkav share watch and honest talk about belonging. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: hush before storm; love and mortality holding hands.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Airlocks
chapters.summary: Remnant gunship and Compact marines clash outside while colonists defend the vault corridor with improvised barricades. Casualties mount. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: chaos and courage; the price of survival being paid in blood.

chapters.title: Odile Falls
chapters.summary: Odile dies holding the vault door's manual override, buying the rite its opening. Her last words are the first line of the confession, learned overnight. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: sacrifice completing atonement; the sinner's granddaughter pays the founding debt.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ansel, voice shaking, delivers the founders' confession in Kessari before both fleets, the core translating and amplifying it across all channels. Fighting falters as every ship hears the truth. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: climax; one borrowed voice carrying two centuries of debt into the light.

chapters.title: The Core Answers
chapters.summary: The vault-core responds: it accepts the confession, powers down its captive song, and releases its archive — proof of the Purge crimes AND of Compact salvage fraud, enough to end the war's justification. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth as disarmament.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at Meridian
chapters.summary: Reyes, exposed by the archive and deserted by her own crew, stands down. Ashkav broadcasts the ceasefire to Remnant command. Guns lower in the dark. POV: Ashkav. Emotional beat: exhausted grace; enemies too spent to be anything but human.

chapters.title: Counting the Cost
chapters.summary: The colony buries its dead, including Odile, beside the opened vault. Three colonists choose to leave with the fleets; the rest stay. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: grief integrated; survival's price itemized and honored.

chapters.title: The Question of Ansel
chapters.summary: Both factions ask who Ansel legally is — clone, heir, or murderer's double. Ansel answers: 'the one who stayed,' and the colony ratifies it in their census. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: identity resolved not by origin but by action; belonging declared.

chapters.title: The Seed-Ship Arrives
chapters.summary: The Kessari seed-ship that sent the signal arrives to reclaim its core, and finds instead a colony that confessed. Its elders offer Meridian a covenant: shared stewardship of the vault. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: wonder after wounds; the forgotten and the extinct adopting each other.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Array
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Sefa and Kessari engineers rebuild the deep-array together, Meridian becoming a listening post between former enemies. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: quiet hope institutionalized; repair as a way of life.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: Ansel formally closes the original's murder case, appending their own testimony, and files the colony's true history where the Core can never bury it again. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: peace with the inherited dead; the record finally telling the truth.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Signal
chapters.summary: Meridian's winter begins, but the station is warm, fuller, and no longer alone. A new transmission arrives — friendly, expected, in two languages. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: earned serenity; the watchers finally watched over.

chapters.title: The Last Vector
chapters.summary: Ansel writes the colony's new charter's opening line — 'We were saved by telling the truth' — and steps out to watch the seed-ship rise. Every vector of their life pointed here. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: resolution; a clone becomes an original by choosing what to carry forward.
